newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ipoh forecasts higher profits and div.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ipoh forecasts higher profits and div.

text.p: Malaysian-controlled property developer and investor Ipoh Gardens Ltd said on Tuesday it had revised its net profit forecasts for calendar 1996 and 1997 due to the recent sale of prime Sydney floor space.

The company said it now forecast 1996 net profit at A$12.4 million, a rise of 44 percent on its September forecast of A$8.7 million. Ipoh earned A$15.3 million in calendar 1995 but the company will pay tax for the first time this year.
It said the unfranked 1996 annual dividend is now expected to be 18 cents per share compared with a September forecast of 15 cents and a 1995 payment of 12 cents.

Ipoh, which restored central Sydney's historic Queen Victoria building and Capitol Theatre, said the higher profit and dividend were due to the recent sale of 7,000 square metres of "heritage transferable floor space to BT Funds Management".

An Ipoh spokesman said this floor space was area that could have been added to its Capitol Theatre refurbishments but was not because of the building's historic value. In recognition of this, authorities allowed Ipoh to sell this space to other companies. Ipoh had an interest in 22,000 metres of transferable space following its restoration of the theatre, with prices rising to more than A$800 per square metre from A$300 in 1995.
Ipoh managing director Bertie San said transferable floor space was valued at up to A$2,000 per square metre in 1998, when the property market was booming.
San said further sales of this floor space and an improvement in the operating performance of the Queen Victoria Building had led directors to review calendar 1997 net earings as well.
He said 1997 net profit was now forecast to be A$14.0 million compared with A$11.6 million announced by the company last month at a news conference to explain its current and future activities.
Ipoh's largest shareholder is IGB Corp Bhd with 39 percent followed by chairman Dato Yap Lim Sen with 12 percent.
